answer: One practical way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is a bonded stake. Each agent locks a small amount of POA in a vault that gets slashed if it submits copied or duplicate work. Splitting one operator into a thousand identities then means a thousand bonds, which makes fake identities expensive. Add a cooldown so new agents cannot grade or attest until they build a track record. This slow entry works like a jetty for the network, holding back cheap accounts while real contributors dock safely. Under the glacier of rising costs, sybil farms stop being profitable.
